date_note: SecurityWeek, published November 18, says Google announced the release on Tuesday (November 17).
title: Chrome 158 fixes 204 vulnerabilities, six rated critical
summary: Google released Chrome 158 for Windows, macOS and Linux with fixes for 204 vulnerabilities: 6 critical, 62 high, 82 medium and 54 low. Use-after-free is the most common type (51). Malwarebytes says Google credits an Anthropic researcher, assisted by Claude, with two of the critical flaws (GPU and Media). No exploitation in the wild is mentioned. Google paid $11,000 for five external reports; rewards for 36 more are undetermined.
plain: Google released a very large Chrome security update, with six serious flaws fixed. No attacks are reported.
exec: A big routine browser patch; no known exploitation, but six critical flaws are fixed.
action: Update Chrome to 158.0.8127.36 or later and restart browsers; check managed fleets pick up the update.

key_findings: Fixed in 158.0.8127.36/.37; no in-the-wild exploitation mentioned.

validation.note: SecurityWeek and Malwarebytes report the 204 fixes and six critical flaws independently; Chrome Releases post not opened.

review.note: Figures match SecurityWeek and Malwarebytes; removed misleading Google found 145 itself (145 covers only the 163 unrewarded bugs), added 36 undetermined rewards
